observedBehaviour: DocumentTableCell.node(...) accepts any DocumentNode, but in 2.2.0 only three kinds actually draw their content in the cell: ParagraphNode, ListNode and a nested TableNode. RowNode, ShapeContainerNode and CanvasLayerNode reserve the cell's height and draw none of their child content at all. SectionNode and LayerStackNode are worse to diagnose than either: they draw part of it — measured at 0.4 of the ink the same child draws in plain page flow — so the cell looks populated and is quietly truncated. Nothing is thrown and no warning is printed; the table is structurally correct and the content is simply not there. It is also invisible to the layout tree, because cell content does not appear in layoutSnapshot() by name, so the only signal is rendered ink.

minimalReproduction.arrangement: Each node kind built twice, with and without leaf text, rendered both in plain page flow and in a one-cell table, rasterised and counted. Subtracting the without-leaf render removes the node's own chrome, so what is compared is the leaf's own ink in the two placements.

workaround: Keep cell content to the three kinds that survive: DocumentTableCell.text(...) for one logical value, DocumentTableCell.lines(...) for an explicit multiline value, and DocumentTableCell.node(ParagraphNode) when the value needs styling or inline runs. A nested TableNode is the supported route for structure inside a cell. Do not reach for a Section, Row, ShapeContainer, LayerStack or CanvasLayer to arrange a cell's insides — the arrangement will look right in the code and be missing on the page. Where a cell genuinely needs two-dimensional arrangement, use a nested table, or take the content out of the table and place it with the page's own layout primitives.

sourceRun.note: Reported from a real acceptance run and reproduced here independently. The probe found more than was reported: the partial-draw cases (Section, LayerStack) were not in the original account, and they are the ones that mislead, because a half-drawn cell reads as a styling problem rather than a lost-content one.

retiredNote: Fixed in 2.2.1 for a table in a PLAIN PAGE FLOW, which is the only arrangement `table-cell-node` builds. Re-running it against 2.2.1 shows all eight node kinds drawing in full: contentDrawnInFull became [ParagraphNode, ListNode, TableNode, SectionNode, RowNode, LayerStackNode, ShapeContainerNode, CanvasLayerNode], with contentPartiallyDrawn and contentLost both empty; the same probe reports the same eight on released 2.2.2. On 2.2.0 a RowNode, ShapeContainerNode or CanvasLayerNode in a cell reserved the cell's height and drew none of its child content, and a SectionNode or LayerStackNode drew about 0.4 of the ink. The workaround above is what a project still pinned to 2.2.0 needs. The nested placement has now been measured too. `table-cell-node` grew a second arm on 2026-08-28 — the same one-cell table in the wide column of a two-column row, which is where a sidebar page puts it — and on released 2.2.1 and 2.2.2 all eight kinds draw in full THERE AS WELL: nestedContentLost and nestedContentPartiallyDrawn are both empty. So the fix does reach a cell one level deeper, and this retirement covers both placements. What the same run settled is where the contrary report came from. A create run pinned to 2.2.1-SNAPSHOT reported a composite drawing its box and none of its children inside a row cell, and filed it as a defect surviving the fix. Measured against that exact jar — sha1 a18aa0f12a0fca390fe2088e5cf562ba0089b723, 4108 bytes, a local mvn install — the probe reproduces THIS record's 2.2.0 numbers exactly, at both placements: ParagraphNode, ListNode and TableNode in full, SectionNode and LayerStackNode partial, RowNode, ShapeContainerNode and CanvasLayerNode lost. That jar is pre-fix. It is also the same jar on which `layered-row-survives-a-row-cell` measured layeredRowHorizontal false while 2.2.2 measures it true. A SNAPSHOT named for a release is not that release, and on this machine it was the older code: a run that sees the 2.2.0 behaviour on a build called 2.2.1-SNAPSHOT has found a stale jar, not a new defect.
